references.observation: The BTW model propagates local topplings through four neighbors and has a recognizable deterministic lattice appearance.
references.principle: Display stable heights as discrete pigments rather than artificially illustrating fractal shapes.
references.application: Exact four/eight-neighbor redistribution in a 161 by 161 grid, rendered as integer square cells.
references.avoid: Do not copy encyclopedia photographs, color maps, illustrations or text descriptions.

references.observation: A black and white tile rule turns a moving ant and eventually produces a repeating directional highway.
references.principle: Let deterministic stepping expose structure rather than prepainting trails or predicting outcomes.
references.application: Changeable R/L rule strings, multi-ant positions and direct injections on a bounded periodic grid.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce the exact Wolfram screenshots or branded graph presentation.

references.observation: Gray-Scott reaction diffusion updates two local concentration fields and varied feed and kill constants yield spots, splitting cells and coral patterns.
references.principle: Provide distinct feed/kill presets but keep the real numerical update continuously visible.
references.application: Directly seed reagent B and adjust Gray-Scott constants with named preset choices.
references.avoid: Do not copy Karl Sims's rendered media, specific lighting effects or page structure.

concepts.medium: Pure cell-grid Canvas 2D on a mineral instrument panel with a geometric icon authored in editable SVG.
concepts.composition: One square observation stage dominates and splits into two specimens vertically on phones.
concepts.interaction: Inject local disturbances and fork the entire current state by changing one law in a second universe.
concepts.motion: Every pixel change is a mathematically calculated simulation step; restrained immediate mechanical control response.
concepts.rationale: Selected because the user primarily wants uninterrupted observation, simple knobs and rigorous emergence.

concepts.medium: Mechanical procedural SVG schematic with thousands of real physical tile objects and a rotating crank.
concepts.composition: A circular apparatus with radial controls replaces the uninterrupted square canvas.
concepts.interaction: Turn a crank to add grains manually and push physical levers between toppling modes.
concepts.motion: Individual tiles physically lift and lower using timed interpolation and metallic mechanical feedback.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because dimensional ornament and per-tile DOM animation would obscure large grid dynamics and slow mobile phones.

concepts.medium: Illustrated archival notebook with static cell diagrams and transition panels arranged into chapter pages.
concepts.composition: A two-column visual taxonomy and explanatory captions rather than an immersive simulation instrument.
concepts.interaction: Turn illustrated chapters, reveal scientific explanations and compare saved images without manipulating live rules.
concepts.motion: Paper chapter folding and sequential gallery transitions carry navigation rather than computational time.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because written exposition would compete with the explicitly requested visual observation.

selection.reason: The real-time specimen is the most meaningful image and two simultaneous live worlds give an immediate experimental counterfactual.

rejected.reason: A large mechanical crank makes interaction decorative and adds latency to what should be instant mathematical stepping.
Explanatory folio pages are static and prevent direct exploration, which is the user's primary goal.

tools.reason: Handwritten app-owned SVG source is supported by the browser and has already been authored as editable vector geometry.
Canvas 2D ImageData and deterministic JavaScript state allow actual simulation output with no external assets.

assets.role: Four-direction redistribution is translated into a distinctive centered plus-shaped icon with four colored receiver cells.
assets.acceptance: The four-lobe redistribution silhouette must remain readable at 48 CSS pixels and be different from the previous particle app icon.
assets.integration: The exported SVG is loaded through the document icon link and scoped PWA manifest without external requests.
assets.provenance: Original geometric SVG authored specifically for this app with no third-party imagery.

risks: On a short iPhone the two square worlds may become too small; verify practical split viewing.
ImageData updates and sandpile topplings may exceed the frame budget on weak mobile devices.
comparisons: Compare initial stage area against Bzyn's portrait framed board.
Compare mathematical split specimens against Press's desktop file-processing two-column ledger.
